question: If a sum of ₹9,10,000 is invested for a year at 2% per annum compounded half yearly, then find the compound interest.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **half-yearly compounding**, the rate becomes 1% (2% ÷ 2) and time becomes 2 periods.

Effective rate for 2 periods at 1% = 1 + 1 + (1 × 1)/100 = **2.01%**.

Compound Interest = 2.01% of ₹9,10,000

CI = 2.01 × 9,100 = ₹18,291.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹18,291.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹9,10,000

Annual Rate (R) = 2%

Time (T) = 1 year

Since the interest is **compounded half-yearly**:

⇒ Half-yearly rate (r) = 2% ÷ 2 = 1%

⇒ Number of conversion periods (n) = 1 × 2 = 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/20841a15daeef95b6be3badb6ec1e3351d1997a7eb6a2a29015d29fac4e20d50.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 9,10,000 × (1 + 1/100)²

⇒ A = 9,10,000 × (101/100) × (101/100)

⇒ A = 91 × 101 × 101

⇒ A = 91 × 10,201

⇒ A = ₹9,28,291

⇒ CI = 9,28,291 − 9,10,000

⇒ CI = ₹18,291

**∴ The correct answer is ₹18,291.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate for Compounding

When interest is compounded **k times** a year, the effective annual rate is (1 + R/(100×k))k − 1.

CI − SI Difference

For 2 periods, the difference between **Compound Interest** and **Simple Interest** is given by P(r/100)².

Half-Yearly vs Quarterly

In half-yearly compounding, rate is R/2 and time is 2T. In quarterly compounding, rate is R/4 and time is 4T.
